scope: Independent rendered-pixel review of NameSnap's in-app web purchase and restoration entry dialogs. This is not approval of live payment processing, email delivery, deployment, or hosted Stripe Checkout.

categoryEvidence.audienceResonance: phone.png: a single email and two plan actions suit a lightweight picker purchase; the prominent playful heading consumes more space than a strictly transactional form.
categoryEvidence.categoryRecognition: desktop.png and plan-component.png: currency amounts, billing intervals, email field, and purchase actions are recognizable; the form is a pre-checkout plan choice rather than a payment collection screen.
categoryEvidence.productSpecificity: phone.png: contestant-limit language and the established double-outline style identify the picker context, though the modal itself does not repeat the NameSnap wordmark.
categoryEvidence.primaryTaskClarity: phone.png: the required email field precedes both priced actions; payment handoff text explicitly identifies Stripe.
categoryEvidence.visualHierarchy: desktop.png: heading, email, and colored plan actions form a clear sequence; the headline remains visually heavier than the small billing disclosure.
categoryEvidence.compositionDiversity: restore.png replaces the paired plan choices with an email recovery action; modal framing remains intentionally consistent with purchase.
categoryEvidence.contentRealism: plan-component.png: $6.99 one-time and $0.99 monthly values agree with their labels; buyer@example.com in state renders is a test fixture rather than a real purchaser.
categoryEvidence.domainArtifactFidelity: desktop.png: actual purchase options and required email occupy the operational center; only a small brand sparkle is decorative.
categoryEvidence.crossScreenContinuity: email-component.png, checkout-error.png, and restore.png retain the entered purchase email; hosted Stripe and paid-return pixels are outside this review.
categoryEvidence.platformFidelity: phone.png, tablet.png, desktop.png: the complete dialog stays within each captured viewport and purchase controls are not clipped; behavior with an open mobile keyboard was not shown.
categoryEvidence.spatialEconomy: phone.png: both plan options remain side by side and the whole purchase decision fits; desktop maintains generous secondary-copy spacing.
categoryEvidence.typography: phone.png and plan-component.png: entered email, prices, and purchase labels are readable; small secondary billing and legal copy remain the main typographic compromise.
categoryEvidence.accessibility: desktop.png: keyboard focus is visible on the close action; labels, large form control, and large plan buttons are evident. Small legal text limits readability. Source review confirms modal keyboard handling but does not replace assistive-technology testing.
categoryEvidence.interactionCredibility: plan-component.png: each plan object combines a purchase verb, price, interval, and a button surface; no selected state misleadingly implies a separate missing continuation action.
categoryEvidence.stateCompleteness: checkout-error.png now gives a comprehensible temporary-unavailability message and retry direction; restore.png provides recovery instructions. Loading and paid-return states were assessed in source/tests rather than rendered here.
categoryEvidence.distinctiveness: plan-component.png and desktop.png preserve the recognizable outlined controls and restrained playful color without adding unrelated dashboard decoration.
categoryEvidence.appStorePlausibility: phone.png: complete production-style dialog with real fields, prices, recovery, and legal navigation; this is web UI rather than a store screenshot marketing frame.
categoryEvidence.implementationReadiness: isolated component renders correspond to implemented labels, email field, plan buttons, state messages, and responsive CSS; independent payment regression work remains separately tracked.
categoryEvidence.componentSemantics: restore.png: Send restore link and Check purchase on this browser now name different operations, while sales and renewal copy are removed from the recovery task.
categoryEvidence.materialFit: phone.png and desktop.png: playful gradients, dark outlines, and shallow colored offsets fit the picker brand; hierarchy and contrast remain readable.

blurTest.evidence: Across phone, tablet, and desktop, a form followed by two large priced-choice blocks remains the dominant purchase structure.

silhouetteTest.evidence: Paired purchase options and single-action recovery form use different internal compositions; no generic dashboard or marketing-preview skeleton is imported.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: Required purchase email, Unlock Lifetime, Go Monthly, and the visible dollar amounts identify the next action in phone.png and desktop.png.

realityTest.evidence: Real prices, billing intervals, explicit web-versus-App-Store scope, restoration, errors, and legal navigation replace placeholder UI.

journeyTest.evidence: Email remains present through the captured error and recovery views, and the restored-state controls distinguish email recovery from checking this browser. This covers the captured pre-checkout journey only.

platformTest.evidence: Phone, tablet, and desktop artifacts show no clipped primary controls or horizontal overflow; close and plan actions have clear boundaries and visible focus.

buyerValueTest.evidence: The rendered dialog presents actionable paid choices and required information rather than a wireframe, template preview, or planning slide.

implementationTest.evidence: The rendered email and plan components map to explicit implemented fields, buttons, CSS states, and checkout handlers; no decorative control lacks a corresponding action.

componentSemanticTest.evidence: Price, interval, and action agree inside both isolated plan components; revised recovery controls have distinct labels and purposes.

categoryReferenceTest.evidence: Current Stripe, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle sources were reviewed for email collection, identifiable purchase details, hosted/overlay checkout handoff, and recovery grammar. NameSnap retains its own established visual treatment. No device frame, promotional screenshot overlay, traceable template copying, or unrelated category convention appears in the captured UI.

references.comparison: Explicit purchase details, email collection, responsive checkout, and comprehensible errors.
Focused hosted/overlay payment handoff with product information and customer email.
Software purchase confidence, branded cross-device checkout, and post-purchase recovery.

screenFindings.finding: Complete purchase dialog fits 390px width; prices and email are readable, with small secondary legal/billing text.
Same phone purchase capture confirms paired plan layout and aligned button boundaries.
Email and paired plans retain their hierarchy with no clipped labels.
Centered dialog preserves scope, pricing, and visible focus; headline is intentionally prominent.
Revised recovery subtitle and distinct controls remove purchase/restore ambiguity.
Revised temporary-unavailability error retains the email and leaves plan controls available for retry.
Explicit required label, 16px entered email, help text, and consistent input boundary.
Both purchase actions show matching price and billing interval without overlap.

repairs.resolution: Re-rendered checkout-error.png shows a clear temporary-unavailability message and retry instruction.

repairs.issue: Competing restore action labels and purchase promotion within restore
repairs.resolution: Re-rendered restore.png distinguishes Send restore link from Check purchase on this browser, changes the subtitle to recovery, and removes renewal sales copy.

limitations: Hosted Stripe Checkout and live email delivery were not visually validated in this review.
Backend uncertain-response recovery and cross-browser idempotency are separate release checks.
Mobile keyboard-open, screen-reader, and browser-zoom variants were not captured.
verdict: PASS for the captured NameSnap purchase and restore dialog pixels after the targeted repairs. The overall score is 93.8/100 and every category is at least 9.0. Live payment, restoration email delivery, and backend release approval remain separate.
